Description: Entry point for the tool. A library is a collection of catalogs; a catalog is a collection of items that share one set of properties and one set of unit types. Two scopes run through everything here and must never be confused: your view (which libraries are on your tabs, per user, non-destructive) and the data (shared by everyone).
Which libraries a person keeps on their tabs, in the order they added them. Changing it never touches the data.

Title 3: Switch between my libraries with tabs
Description: As a user, I want my libraries as tabs above the catalog list, so that moving between the ones I use is one click rather than a navigation.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The panel below the tabs is welded to the active tab, so the two read as one folder.
- Selecting a tab shows that library's catalogs.
- Which libraries are open, and which is active, are saved per user and restored on return.

Title 3: Take a library off my tabs without deleting it
Description: As a user, I want to dismiss a library from my own tabs, so that my view holds only what I use, without affecting anyone else.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The x on a tab removes that library from my view only. Nothing is deleted and no one else is affected.
- The x is disabled on the last open tab — the page always shows a library.
- The dismissed library can be added back from the picker at any time.

Title 3: Add a library to my view from a picker
Description: As a user, I want a searchable picker of every library, so that I can pull one in when I occasionally need it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The + on the tab strip opens the picker with focus in the search field, so it is typeable immediately.
- The list narrows as I type.
- Libraries already on my tabs are marked 'In your view'.
- Choosing an option adds it to my tabs and switches to it.
- Escape or a click outside closes without changing my view.

Title 3: Create a library from the picker when none matches
Description: As a user, I want to create a library from the picker when my typed name matches nothing, so that I do not have to leave the flow to add one.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A Create "<name>" option appears only when the typed name matches no existing library.
- Choosing it creates the library and opens it.
- The new library appears in the picker for everyone.

Title 3: Work the library picker from the keyboard
Description: As a user, I want to drive the picker without the mouse, so that adding a library stays as fast as typing its name.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Down from the field enters the list, then walks it; Up walks back and returns to the field from the top.
- Enter or Tab takes the focused option.
- Tab is only intercepted while an option has focus, so it still leaves the picker from the field.
- Escape closes the picker.

Description: The library itself — its name, the stock forms it allows, its catalogs, and its deletion. These are shared data, so every destructive action names what goes with it.

Title 3: Rename a library in Library Settings
Description: As a user, I want to rename a library, so that it is findable by the name people actually use for it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The pencil beside the library name opens the Library Settings flyout.
- Renaming updates the tab, the panel title and the picker.
- An empty name is refused: the field takes the error tint and a toast says why.
- Cancel, the overlay and Escape all discard the draft cleanly.

Title 3: Set which stock forms a library allows
Description: As a user, I want to say which physical forms stock takes in a library, so that a library of laptops is never offered 'roll'.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Library Settings lists Roll, Piece, Sheet and Non-Depletable as switches.
- Help text reads: the physical forms stock takes in this library. Catalog unit types can only use forms listed here.
- A library needs at least one stock form — the last one on cannot be turned off, and says why (R14).
- A form already in use by a unit type stays listed in that type's Stock Form select even if the library has since dropped it (R15).
- The setting persists and is read by the catalog settings page.

Title 3: Delete a library and be told what goes with it
Description: As a user, I want deleting a library to state its real scope before it happens, so that I never confuse hiding with deleting.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The trash beside the pencil opens a confirmation modal.
- The body states the catalog count and says the catalogs are deleted too, for everyone.
- The modal points at the tab x as the way to only remove it from my own view (R4).
- The trash is disabled when only one library exists.
- Cancel, x, Escape and the overlay all close with nothing deleted.

Title 3: Add a catalog to a library
Description: As a user, I want to add a catalog to the open library, so that a new group of stock has somewhere to live.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add Catalog creates a catalog in the active library.
- A catalog needs a name before it appears in the list.
- A library needs at least one catalog — deleting the library is how the last one is removed (R2).

Title 3: Open a catalog or its settings from the library list
Description: As a user, I want the catalog row to open its items and the pencil to open its settings, so that both are reachable without a menu.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The whole row opens the catalog's item list.
- The pencil on the row opens that catalog's settings.
- The count badge is read-only and shows how many items the catalog holds.

Description: Everything that defines what a catalog's items carry and how its stock is held. The page is a working copy: nothing is committed until Save Changes.
The fields every item in a catalog carries, global and created.

Title 3: Keep the global properties on every catalog
Description: As a user, I want Vendor, Default Location, Product Line, Family and Color present and non-removable, so that the rest of Platinum always has something to join on.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The five global property chips appear on every catalog.
- They carry no remove affordance.
- They are visually distinct from properties the catalog created.

Title 3: Add a catalog property with a type
Description: As a user, I want to add a property and choose its type, so that items can record the facts this catalog actually needs.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add Catalog Property takes a name and a type: True/False, Dropdown, Measurement, Number or Description.
- A dropdown property also takes its options.
- Each chip carries the icon of its type: toggle, diamond, square, hashtag, text.
- Per-item facts such as a die's last job belong here rather than as bespoke columns.

Title 3: Remove a property and be told what is lost
Description: As a user, I want removing a property to say what goes with it, so that I do not silently discard recorded values.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The x on a created chip removes the property from the catalog.
- It states that values recorded on existing items are lost (R6).
- Nothing is committed until Save Changes.

Title 3: Save or cancel the whole settings page at once
Description: As a user, I want the settings page to commit as one thing, so that a half-made change never reaches the catalog.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Save Changes commits the title, properties, unit types and naming together.
- The button is disabled until something actually changes.
- It confirms in place, then returns to rest.
- Cancel returns to the item list; nothing committed is lost, because nothing was committed.

Title 3: Rename a catalog where naming happens
Description: As a user, I want the catalog's name edited as a labeled field on its settings page, so that renaming is not hidden behind an edit affordance.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Catalog Title is a normal field at the top of the settings page.
- Renaming here renames the catalog on the item list and in its library once saved.

Description: A unit type is a named way an item is held. Its stock form is the shape behind it, and the shape decides which fields a unit records.

Title 3: Read a unit type's shape at a glance
Description: As a user, I want each unit type summarized in one line, so that I can see what a unit of it records without opening anything.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The row shows name, stock form with its icon, the fields a unit records, and a worked example.
- Rolls read as Roll Width (inches) x Length (yards), i.e. 64 yards.
- Sheets read as Width x Height and Count, i.e. 35 sheets (8.5 x 11 inches).
- Clicking the row is a shortcut to Edit; the buttons are the keyboard path.

Title 3: Add or edit a unit type in a flyout
Description: As a user, I want unit types edited in a flyout over a draft, so that backing out never leaves a half-made type behind.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add Unit Type opens the flyout empty, defaulted to a piece.
- The flyout uses the same overlay and panel recipe as Edit Job Details.
- Save Unit Type writes the draft into the page's working config — still not committed until Save Changes.
- Cancel, x, Escape and the overlay discard the draft.

Title 3: Name a unit type, or let the stock form name it
Description: As a user, I want to call a unit type what we call it, and to get a sensible name if I do not, so that naming is never a blocker.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit type name accepts anything — Rolls, Miscuts, Swatches.
- Left blank, it falls back to the stock form's default name.
- Switching the stock form renames the type if it still carries the old default name.

Title 3: Choose the units a roll or sheet records
Description: As a user, I want each dimension to carry its own unit, so that a 54 inch wide roll of 50 yards reads correctly.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A roll takes a width unit and a length unit separately; stock is the length, not a headcount of rolls.
- A sheet takes a width unit and a height unit separately, because 8.5 x 11 in and 40 x 60 in are both real; stock is the count.
- A piece takes no units; stock is the count.
- Switching the stock form swaps the whole field set.

Title 3: Give a unit type default values
Description: As a user, I want new units to start with the measurements most of them have, so that adding one is a confirmation rather than a transcription.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Edit Unit Type has a Default Values group covering whatever the stock form measures: Width and Yardage for a roll, Width, Height and Count for a sheet, Count for a piece.
- Job Number and Location never take a default (R13).
- A field with no default starts empty on a new row, showing its placeholder.
- Defaults are stored on unitType.defaults and saved with the rest of the config.
- A dimension of zero is not a default and is dropped on save.

Title 3: Delete a unit type with an in-place confirmation
Description: As a user, I want deleting a unit type to confirm in the row and name what goes with it, so that a dialog is not needed for a small decision.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The trash turns the row into a confirmation naming the unit type and how many recorded units go with it.
- Delete removes it from the working copy; Cancel and Escape back out.
- The trash is disabled on the last unit type — a catalog needs at least one way to hold stock (R1), and says why.

Title 3: Only offer stock forms the library allows
Description: As a user, I want a catalog's stock forms limited to its library's, so that unit types cannot drift outside what the library is for.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The Stock Form select lists only the forms the library allows.
- A form already in use by this unit type stays listed even if the library has since dropped it (R15).
- A new unit type defaults to piece when the library allows it, otherwise to the library's first form.

Description: Item names are generated from a template of properties, never typed.

Title 3: Build item names from a segment template
Description: As a user, I want item names composed from properties in order, so that every item in a catalog is named the same way (R8).
Acceptance Criteria:
- Segment chips show the template in order — Vendor, Product Line, Family, Color reads as Majilite-Majilite-Baby Ostrich-Cobalt Blue.
- Add Naming Segment appends a property to the end of the template.
- Only properties this catalog carries can be segments.
- The x on a segment drops it from the template.
- Item names are never typed by hand.

Description: The item list and the rollup: the read surfaces that answer how much of something there is, and whether it needs attention.
One row per item, the four standard figures across it, per unit type.

Title 3: See every item's figures for one unit type
Description: As a user, I want the item list to report On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available, so that I can judge stock without opening an item.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit type tabs switch which unit type the table reports on.
- Every tab shows the same five columns; only the measure in the headers changes, because a roll is counted in yards and a piece is not counted in anything.
- Available is derived as In-House minus Allocated and is never stored, so no figure can contradict another.
- The item name opens the item page; the whole row is the target, and the name keeps a real link for middle-click and new-tab.

Title 3: Search the item list by name or swatch number
Description: As a user, I want to narrow the list as I type, so that finding one item in eight hundred is immediate.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Search acts on the whole list, live, and sits on the page rather than on the table's surface.
- A count appears only while the search is narrowing the list.
- An empty result says so in the table.

Title 3: Sort the item list by any column
Description: As a user, I want to sort by a column, so that the lowest available or the largest on order comes to the top.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A column header sorts ascending, then descending on a second click.
- The caret shows direction; unsorted columns show the resting sort affordance so it is clear they can be clicked.
- Blanks sort to the bottom in both directions — an unknown is not a small number.
- The table opens unsorted, in the order the catalog is kept in.

Description: Colour on a figure means one thing only, and never appears as decoration.

Title 3: Be warned when an item is low or oversold
Description: As a user, I want low and oversold stock marked, so that a reprint is not planned against stock that is not there.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Amber means running low: available at or under 20 percent of in-house. Red means oversold: available below zero (R5).
- The state marks the figure, not the whole cell — a tinted cell would read as a column of its own.
- Both states carry an icon and a tooltip saying which state it is, so neither relies on colour alone.
- No other condition is ever shown in colour.

Title 3: See the four figures for the unit type on an item
Description: As a user, I want a rollup above each unit type's table, so that the headline figures sit with the rows they are made of.
Acceptance Criteria:
- On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available appear as four tiles.
- The tiles are identical by default; colour appears only on Available.
- Each unit type has its own rollup and its own table, because their columns differ.
- A commit in the table rebuilds the rollup in place, so the two can never disagree.

Title 3: Understand On Order as stock that is not yet findable
Description: As a user, I want a unit with no location to read as On Order, so that recorded stock is never counted as being on the shelf.
Acceptance Criteria:
- On Order is the units of this type with no location.
- In-House is the units with a location.
- Allocated is units with a job number and a location — only stock in hand can be allocated against (R17).
- A unit's quantity is counted once: On Order until it has a location, In-House after (R16).
- A newly added unit shows as On Order until it is placed.

Description: The item page as a working surface: every value in a unit row is a field, and stock is corrected where it is read.
A field that reads as text at rest, becomes a field on hover, and is editable on focus.

Title 3: Edit a unit value in place, with no edit mode
Description: As a user, I want to click a value and type over it, so that correcting stock takes no more than reading it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- At rest a field reads exactly as a static cell: no border, no fill, column alignment kept, measurements in settled form (1.50, not 1.5).
- Hovering a row outlines every field in it at once; the field under the pointer takes the stronger edge.
- Focus gives white fill, a focus ring, and selects the contents so typing replaces the value.
- A second click, or a drag, positions the caret normally.
- Commit is blur or Enter; Escape reverts. There are no save or cancel buttons.

Title 3: Be stopped from typing a value that cannot be right
Description: As a user, I want the field to refuse characters that do not belong, so that most mistakes never happen.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Numeric fields accept digits only; decimals take a single point and two places. No steppers.
- Job Number is digits-only and capped at six characters.
- Location is free text, capped at a sensible length.
- Characters that do not belong simply never land.

Title 3: Have an invalid entry rejected outright and told why
Description: As a user, I want a rejected value to snap back with a reason, so that I am never left with a half-accepted entry.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The field returns to the value it held (R9).
- The error tint flashes just long enough to point at which field refused.
- A toast names the reason — for example, job numbers are six digits.
- Empty placeholders read in the field's own shape (000000, 0.00, 0, Add location) in tertiary text, replacing the old plus button.

Title 3: Have clearing a number left alone, and clearing a job mean something
Description: As a user, I want an emptied number to revert silently and an emptied job number to release the allocation, so that each field does what its value means.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Emptying a number is not an entry: it reverts to what it held, with no telling off.
- Emptying Job Number releases the allocation, replacing the old x action.
- Allocated and Available follow immediately.

Title 3: Tab through a row without the table moving underneath me
Description: As a user, I want the figures to follow my edits without the rows being re-rendered, so that I can work a row field by field.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A commit rebuilds the rollup and the footer in place.
- Neither the rollup nor the footer holds a field, so the table stands and focus is kept.
- Tab moves to the next field in the row.

Description: Committing a unit to a job, and releasing it.

Title 3: Allocate a unit to a job
Description: As a user, I want to put a job number on a unit, so that stock committed to work is not offered to anyone else.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A job number is exactly six digits (R7).
- Committing a job number moves Allocated and Available immediately.
- Only a placed unit can be allocated (R17).
- Switching unit type tabs mid-edit abandons an open field, so it never reappears against a different unit type.

Title 3: Print a unit label
Description: As a user, I want to print a label for a unit, so that what is on the shelf carries its own identity.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every unit row has a print action at its trailing edge.
- Row actions appear on hover and on focus-within.

Description: A new unit is entered in the same place, and the same way, an existing one is corrected.

Title 3: Add a unit as a row rather than a form
Description: As a user, I want Add to append a row and put the cursor in it, so that there is one way to enter stock, not two.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add Roll / Add Sheet / Add Swatch appends a row at the bottom of the table and focuses its first field.
- There is no modal and no separate form.
- The unit type's default values are filled in; fields with no default start empty.
- Location starts empty, so a new unit reads as On Order until it is placed.
- An un-entered quantity is not depletion, so the new row stays put while it is being filled.

Description: A quantity of zero is depletion, not an error.

Title 3: Have used-up units leave the table without vanishing mid-edit
Description: As a user, I want a zeroed unit to dim where it stands and only leave once I am out of the row, so that a mistyped zero can be corrected.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Zeroing a quantity dims the row immediately: still readable, still editable, plainly not part of what is on hand.
- The row is only taken off screen once the cursor has left it (R12).
- A toast says where it went.
- Zero is a real quantity for Yardage and Count; dimensions must still be greater than zero (R10, R11).

Title 3: Bring depleted units back when I need them
Description: As a user, I want a Show depleted switch, so that recounting a unit zeroed by mistake is possible.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Show depleted sits inline with the back link, above the first card, and defaults to off.
- It is a labelled control over a real checkbox, so it is keyboard and screen-reader operable.
- The footer says what is on screen and what is being kept off it — '2 units, 1 depleted hidden'.
- Two different empty states: nothing here at all, versus nothing left that is not used up, which points at the switch.

Description: A fourth stock form for stock that is never used up and is only ever somewhere. It records no measurement and no quantity: one record is one asset, and its location is the whole of the stock story.
The stock form, its tracking setting, and the identity field.

Title 3: Choose Non-Depletable as a stock form
Description: As a user, I want a stock form for things that are only ever moved, so that laptops and dies are not forced into a quantity they do not have.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Non-Depletable appears beside Roll, Sheet and Piece wherever stock forms are listed.
- Choosing it replaces the flyout's measurement fields entirely — no width, no length, no unit selects.
- A note states that non-depletable stock records no quantity: one record is one asset, and its location is what makes it allocated or available.
- Default Values are absent by design: the form's only two fields are the two that never take a default (R13).

Title 3: Set whether a non-depletable type is single or multiple units
Description: As a user, I want to say whether a catalog holds many of the same item or many unique ones, so that the tool matches how the stock actually is.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Tracking offers Multiple units and Single unit as two options on screen with their consequences written under them, not as a line in a select.
- Multiple units: many of the same item — the item has a page, its assets live there, and the rollup is on the item.
- Single unit: every item is unique — there is no item page, the item carries its own location, and the rollup sits on the catalog (R20).
- The summary row reads 'Non-Depletable, Multiple units' — the form and the tracking together decide the shape of the catalog.

Title 3: Name the identity field for a non-depletable type
Description: As a user, I want to call the identity what we call it, so that a row reads as an asset tag, a die number or a serial.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Identity field takes a label and defaults by tracking: Asset Tag for multiple units, Item Number for single.
- Changing the tracking updates the label only while it still carries the other one's default.
- The label is used as the first column header on the item or catalog table.

Title 2: Location as the whole stock story
Description: Locations are typed, and the type is what makes an asset allocated or available.

Title 3: Pick a location from a list grouped by what it means
Description: As a user, I want the location picker grouped into Stock Room and Assigned, so that the consequence of a choice is visible while I make it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The picker groups locations as Stock Room and Assigned, plus 'Not placed'.
- The cell rests as plain text and only shows a border and caret once the row is hovered or focused.
- It commits on change — a select has nothing to type, so there is nothing to correct first.
- A toast names the asset and where it went.
- Only the rollup is rebuilt; the table stands, so the cursor is never pulled out of a row mid-move.

Title 3: Get the four standard figures from locations alone
Description: As a user, I want On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available for non-depletable stock, so that it reports the same way everything else does.
Acceptance Criteria:
- On Order is records with no location; In-House is records with one, wherever it is.
- Allocated is records whose location is in the Assigned group; Available is In-House minus Allocated (R19).
- Figures are counted in assets and shown in 'ea'.
- Low and oversold marking on Available behaves exactly as it does for measured stock (R5).

Title 3: See a status rather than infer it from a location name
Description: As a user, I want a status column, so that I do not have to know the cage to know a machine is available.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each row states On order, Allocated or Available (for dies: On order, In use, On the rack).
- The pill is neutral in every state — an assigned laptop is not a problem, it is simply not available to issue.
- The pill carries an icon and a tooltip explaining the state.

Description: Many of the same item, each one an asset in its own right.

Title 3: Track every laptop of one model on its item page
Description: As a user in IT, I want each machine of a model listed with its tag and location, so that I know how many are free and who has the rest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The item page shows the rollup and a table of Asset Tag, Location and Status.
- There is no quantity column: the row exists, so the count is one (R18).
- There is no Show depleted switch, because nothing here depletes.
- Add Asset appends a row, focuses its tag, and starts it unplaced so it reads as On Order.

Title 3: Keep asset identities required and unique
Description: As a user, I want a tag that cannot be blank or duplicated, so that a row always names exactly one machine.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An emptied identity is rejected: the field snaps back, the tint flashes, and a toast says every asset needs one (R21).
- A tag already in use on another record is rejected the same way, naming the clash.
- Typing is constrained to the identity's shape as it happens.

Title 3: See a non-depletable catalog list the same as any other
Description: As a user, I want the catalog of laptops to look like the catalog of bookcloth, so that nothing new has to be learned to read it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- One row per item with On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available, counted in ea.
- Search and sort behave as they do on a measured catalog.
- The item name drills into that item's assets.
- A catalog with one unit type shows no tab strip — a single tab is a control that cannot be used.

Description: One item is one asset, so the item is the unit.

Title 3: Work a catalog of unique items without item pages
Description: As a user in bindery, I want the die catalog itself to be the working surface, so that I am not opening a page to see a single row.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The rollup sits at the top of the catalog page, above the search that filters the table beneath it.
- One row per item: identity, item name, location and status.
- The item name is not a link — there is nowhere for it to go (R20).
- Location is the one editable value on the page.

Title 3: Find a unique item by number, name or where it is
Description: As a user, I want to search a single-unit catalog by location too, so that 'what is on the Kluge' is one search.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Search matches identity, item name and location label.
- Sorting is available on every column; blanks sort to the bottom both ways.
- A count appears only while the search is narrowing the list.

Title 3: Add a unique item as a row
Description: As a user, I want Add Die to append a row and focus its number, so that adding a unique item matches how everything else is entered.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add appends a row at the bottom and focuses the identity field.
- The new item starts unplaced, so it reads as On Order.
- Any search in force is cleared so the new row is visible.

Title 3: Record per-item facts as catalog properties, not columns
Description: As a user, I want facts like a die's last job or its size to be catalog properties, so that the table stays the same everywhere and each catalog still records what it needs.
Acceptance Criteria:
- No bespoke columns are added for one catalog's facts.
- A property added in Catalog Settings is available on the item.
- This is the answer for anything a specific catalog wants to remember about an item.

Description: Rules and components that hold across every surface of the tool.

Title 3: Be told what a destructive action takes with it
Description: As a user, I want every deletion to name its scope first, so that I never learn what was lost afterwards.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Deleting a library names its catalogs; deleting a unit type names its units; removing a property names the recorded values (R6).
- Hiding is per user and reversible; deleting is for everyone and asks first (R4).
- Nothing in the UI lets those two be confused.

Title 3: Get feedback in a toast rather than an alert
Description: As a user, I want short, non-blocking feedback, so that a message never interrupts what I am typing.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Toasts appear top-right in error, success and info kinds.
- Each carries an icon plus a message, never colour alone.
- They auto-dismiss.
- Available to any page as window.toast(message, kind).

Title 3: Operate every control from the keyboard
Description: As a user who works by keyboard, I want the pickers, switches, fields and tables reachable and operable, so that the tool does not require a mouse.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Switches are labelled controls over real checkboxes.
- Flyouts trap focus, return it on close, and close on Escape.
- Sortable headers are buttons and carry aria-sort.
- Every field carries an accessible label naming its column.
- Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.
